chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I heard Abu al-Khattab narrating from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Three [people]; none would ignore their rights except for a hypocrite well-known for his hypocrisy: the one with grey hair in Islam, the bearer of the Quran, and the just Imam.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the three people whose rights should not be ignored according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates three distinct categories of authority whose neglect signifies recognized hypocrisy: the elderly Muslim (Dhu al-Shaybah), the Quranic scholar (Hamil al-Qur'an), and the Just Imam. This classification underscores the Shia emphasis on respecting both spiritual lineage and scholarly expertise, linking the preservation of the Quranic text directly to the maintenance of just governance.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions,from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I heard Abu Al-Khattab narrating from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Three (people), none would ignore their rights except for a hypocrite well-known with the hypocrisy – one with old age in Al-Islam, and a bearer (memoriser) of the Quran, and the just Imam<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said that he heard abu al-Khattab narrate from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) the following: “

There are three kinds of people whose rights are not ignored, except by a hypocrite, well-known in hypocrisy: of such people is an old person in Islam, the carrier of the Holy Quran and the Imam who possesses the noble merit of justice.”
